From 36527b9d882362567ceb4eea8666813280f30e6f Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Riwen Lu <luriwen@kylinos.cn>
Date: Tue, 23 Aug 2022 15:43:42 +0800
Subject: [PATCH] ACPI: processor: Remove freq Qos request for all CPUs

The freq Qos request would be removed repeatedly if the cpufreq policy
relates to more than one CPU. Then, it would cause the "called for unknown
object" warning.

Remove the freq Qos request for each CPU relates to the cpufreq policy,
instead of removing repeatedly for the last CPU of it.

Fixes: a1bb46c36ce3 ("ACPI: processor: Add QoS requests for all CPUs")
Reported-by: Jeremy Linton <Jeremy.Linton@arm.com>
Tested-by: Jeremy Linton <jeremy.linton@arm.com>
Signed-off-by: Riwen Lu <luriwen@kylinos.cn>
Cc: 5.4+ <stable@vger.kernel.org> # 5.4+
Signed-off-by: Rafael J. Wysocki <rafael.j.wysocki@intel.com>

diff --git a/drivers/acpi/processor_thermal.c b/drivers/acpi/processor_thermal.c
index db6ac540e924..e534fd49a67e 100644
--- a/drivers/acpi/processor_thermal.c
+++ b/drivers/acpi/processor_thermal.c
@@ -151,7 +151,7 @@ void acpi_thermal_cpufreq_exit(struct cpufreq_policy *policy)
 	unsigned int cpu;
 
 	for_each_cpu(cpu, policy->related_cpus) {
-		struct acpi_processor *pr = per_cpu(processors, policy->cpu);
+		struct acpi_processor *pr = per_cpu(processors, cpu);
 
 		if (pr)
 			freq_qos_remove_request(&pr->thermal_req);
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/acpi/processor_thermal.c`**
   - **Modification**: The line that retrieves the `acpi_processor` structure for the CPU has been changed. Instead of using `policy->cpu`, which refers to the last CPU in the policy, the code now uses `cpu`, which iterates through each CPU in `policy->related_cpus`. This change ensures that the frequency Quality of Service (QoS) request is removed for each CPU related to the cpufreq policy, rather than just the last one.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The modification in `drivers/acpi/processor_thermal.c` addresses a bug where the frequency QoS request was being removed multiple times for the same CPU, leading to warnings about "called for unknown object." By iterating through all CPUs related to the cpufreq policy and removing the QoS request for each one, the patch resolves this issue and prevents the warning from occurring. This change is a direct response to the problem reported by Jeremy Linton and is aimed at improving the stability of the ACPI processor management code.

Here is the commit message:
ACPI: processor: Remove freq Qos request for all CPUs

The freq Qos request would be removed repeatedly if the cpufreq policy
relates to more than one CPU. Then, it would cause the "called for unknown
object" warning.

Remove the freq Qos request for each CPU relates to the cpufreq policy,
instead of removing repeatedly for the last CPU of it.

Fixes: a1bb46c36ce3 ("ACPI: processor: Add QoS requests for all CPUs")
Reported-by: Jeremy Linton <Jeremy.Linton@arm.com>
Tested-by: Jeremy Linton <jeremy.linton@arm.com>
Signed-off-by: Riwen Lu <luriwen@kylinos.cn>
Cc: 5.4+ <stable@vger.kernel.org> # 5.4+
Signed-off-by: Rafael J. Wysocki <rafael.j.wysocki@intel.com>

Here is the root cause:
The bug occurs because the frequency QoS request is removed repeatedly for the last CPU in the cpufreq policy instead of being removed for each CPU related to that policy. This leads to attempts to remove a QoS request for CPUs that may no longer be valid, resulting in the "called for unknown object" warning.

Here is the patch:
 
 void acpi_thermal_cpufreq_exit(struct cpufreq_policy *policy)
 {
 	unsigned int cpu;
 
 	for_each_cpu(cpu, policy->related_cpus) {
-		struct acpi_processor *pr = per_cpu(processors, policy->cpu);
+		struct acpi_processor *pr = per_cpu(processors, cpu);
 
 		if (pr)
 			freq_qos_remove_request(&pr->thermal_req);
 	}
 }
 #else				/* ! CONFIG_CPU_FREQ */

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
struct acpi_processor *pr = per_cpu(processors, policy->cpu);
freq_qos_remove_request(&pr->thermal_req);
```
Reason:
The bug occurs because the code incorrectly uses `policy->cpu`, which refers only to the last CPU in the `cpufreq` policy, leading to repeated removal of the frequency QoS request for that CPU. This results in attempts to remove a QoS request for CPUs that may no longer be valid, causing the "called for unknown object" warning.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
struct acpi_processor *pr = per_cpu(processors, cpu);
freq_qos_remove_request(&pr->thermal_req);
```
Reason:
The fix changes the reference from `policy->cpu` to `cpu`, which iterates over each CPU in `policy->related_cpus`. This ensures that the frequency QoS request is removed for each CPU related to the `cpufreq` policy, preventing the repeated removal for the last CPU and eliminating the warning.
